# Feature Specification: Fix Diet Plan Rendering Crash

**Feature Branch**: `014-fix-diet-meal-render`  
**Created**: 2026-04-06  
**Status**: Draft  
**Input**: Runtime TypeError — `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'charAt')` in DietDayRow when rendering diet plan meals generated by new algorithmic engine

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 — Diet Plan Renders Without Crashing (Priority: P1)

A user with an InBody scan navigates to the Recommendations page and requests a diet plan. The page must display their 7-day meal plan without a runtime crash.

**Why this priority**: The diet plan feature is completely broken for all users. The recommendations page crashes immediately when rendering data from the new algorithmic engine.

**Independent Test**: Generate a diet plan for any user, navigate to the Recommendations page → Diet tab. All 7 days must render with meal names and macro summaries visible — no white screen or console error.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a diet plan generated by the algorithmic engine, **When** the user views the Recommendations page, **Then** all 7 days render with meal names (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Snack) displayed without error
2. **Given** a day row is expanded, **When** meals are shown, **Then** each meal displays its name, food items, and macro totals (calories, protein, carbs, fat)
3. **Given** a diet plan in editing mode, **When** foods are listed, **Then** each food item is shown as a formatted string (e.g. "Chicken breast 150g") with a remove button

---

### User Story 2 — Backwards Compatibility With Old Plans (Priority: P2)

Users who have previously saved or edited diet plans (generated by the old LLM engine) must continue to see their plans render correctly with no regression.

**Why this priority**: Any fix must not break existing user data already stored from prior plan generations.

**Independent Test**: Retrieve an old LLM-format diet plan from the database and render it on the Recommendations page — it must display correctly with no change in appearance.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a stored plan using the old schema (flat `meal.meal` field, `meal.foods` string array), **When** the page renders, **Then** the meal name and foods display correctly
2. **Given** a new plan using the algorithmic schema (`meal.meal_name` field, `meal.items` object array), **When** the page renders, **Then** the meal name and foods also display correctly

---

### Edge Cases

- Meal object has neither `meal` nor `meal_name` — display a fallback label ("Meal")
- `items` array is present but empty — render the meal section with zero macros, no crash
- `meal_totals` is a nested object (new format) instead of flat fields on the meal (old format) — both must display calories/protein/carbs/fat correctly
- Macro fields are undefined or null — all values default to 0, no crash

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: Meal name display MUST fall back gracefully when `meal.meal` is undefined, by also reading `meal.meal_name`; if both are absent, display "Meal"
- **FR-002**: Food items MUST render from either `meal.foods` (string array, old format) or `meal.items` (object array with `food_name` + `grams` fields, new format)
- **FR-003**: Macro totals MUST be read from either flat fields (`meal.calories`, `meal.protein_g`, etc.) or from a nested `meal.meal_totals` object; whichever is present takes precedence
- **FR-004**: All displayed numeric macro values MUST default to 0 if the underlying field is missing or undefined
- **FR-005**: In editing mode, food items from the `items` format MUST render as human-readable strings (e.g. "Chicken breast 150g") consistent with the existing display style for `foods` string arrays

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Zero runtime crashes when rendering diet plans on the Recommendations page — 0 TypeError occurrences
- **SC-002**: Both old LLM-format plans and new algorithmic-format plans render correctly — 100% compatibility rate
- **SC-003**: All 7 days × 4 meals display meal name, food items, and macro values without blank or undefined sections

## Assumptions

- The fix is applied in the frontend rendering layer (the DietDayRow component) to handle both schemas
- The new algorithmic engine output format (`meal_name`, `items`, `meal_totals`) is the going-forward standard
- Food items in the new format always have `food_name` and `grams` fields available
- Existing stored plans in the database may use either format; the fix must handle both transparently
